findings.title: Conditional-serialize hook misnamed so it never runs
findings.body: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153 defines `def include_website_name` without the trailing `?`. ActiveModel::Serializer only honors `include_<attr>?`, as used by every other hook in this file (e.g. `include_email?`, `include_stats?`). As a result the `website.present?` guard is dead code and `website_name` is always serialized, including a `website_name: null` key when there is no website.

findings.title: website_name bypasses TL0 anonymous hiding for website
findings.body: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:105 lists `website` in `untrusted_attributes` so TL0 profiles are hidden from anonymous via `restrict_user_fields?`, but the new `website_name` attribute (added at line 43) was not added there. Since `website_name` is derived directly from `website` (host plus path), an anonymous client can learn a TL0 user's website host/path from `website_name` even when `website` itself is correctly suppressed.

findings.title: Unhandled nil current_hostname crashes user serialization
findings.body: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:139 assigns `discourse_host = Discourse.current_hostname` with no nil guard, then calls `discourse_host.split('.')` at line 144 and `discourse_host.ends_with?` at line 149. If hostname is nil/unset, every UserSerializer render raises NoMethodError, breaking user profile JSON with a 500.

findings.title: Same-domain display drops query, fragment and port
findings.body: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:143 builds the same-domain display as `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`. `URI#path` excludes query string, fragment, and `host` excludes an explicit port, so `http://example.com/user?x=1#y` or `http://example.com:8080/user` is truncated to `example.com/user`, contradicting the PR goal of showing the complete URL path and losing navigation-relevant information.
